summary.en: Build readable conditions using chained comparisons, short-circuit logic, identity and membership.
summary.bn: চেইন তুলনা, শর্ট সার্কিট লজিক, পরিচয় আর সদস্যপদ দিয়ে পড়তে সহজ শর্ত তৈরি করো।

notes: These programs target Python 3.12 and use features available in Python 3.10 or later.

sections.title: Ask a precise question about your values
Stop evaluating when the answer is known
Express a rule and inspect its effect
Equality, identity and membership have different jobs

examples.title: Check the entire marks interval
examples.explanationHtml: A chained comparison checks both boundaries. The second value lies above 100, so its condition is False.

examples.title: Protect a division
examples.explanationHtml: and stops when the left side is false, avoiding division by zero. or returns the first truthy operand, here the fallback text.

examples.title: Equal values and identical objects
examples.explanationHtml: Square brackets create a list, a group of values. The lists have equal contents but are separate objects; alias refers to first itself.

examples.title: Search within text
examples.explanationHtml: String membership looks for an exact, case-sensitive substring. not in reverses the membership result.

practice.title: Valid mark flag
practice.statementHtml: Read an integer mark. Print True if it lies from 0 to 100 inclusive; otherwise print False.
hints: A comparison chain describes the interval directly.

practice.title: Text membership flag
practice.statementHtml: Read a course description. Print True if it contains the exact substring CSE, otherwise False.
hints: The case of the letters matters.

practice.title: Safe ratio threshold
practice.statementHtml: Read an integer numerator and denominator on separate lines. Print True if the denominator is nonzero and the ratio exceeds 2; otherwise print False.
hints: Place the nonzero check before the division in an and expression.

practice.title: Eligibility in two parts
practice.statementHtml: Read age and earned credits on separate lines. Print True when age is at least 18 and credits are at least 30, or when credits are at least 60 regardless of age.
hints: Use parentheses to show how the two eligibility routes combine.

options: A comparison of a bool with 100 only
quiz.explanation: A chain compares adjacent values and requires both comparisons to hold.

quiz.prompt: When does and skip its right operand?
options: When its left operand is truthy
When its left operand is falsey
Whenever the right operand is arithmetic
quiz.explanation: The falsey left result already determines the outcome of and.

quiz.prompt: Which test normally compares two strings by their text?
quiz.explanation: Equality compares values. Identity asks whether the object itself is the same.

quiz.prompt: Which test is idiomatic for absence represented by None?
quiz.explanation: None is a singleton, so identity expresses the intended check.

options: Whether the strings have equal length
quiz.explanation: For str, in asks whether the left string appears inside the right string.

quiz.prompt: What can or return besides True and False?
options: A new bool in every case
quiz.explanation: or returns the first truthy operand, or the last operand if both are falsey.

quiz.prompt: Why should a zero-denominator guard come first in an and expression?
options: It can prevent evaluation of the division
quiz.explanation: The guard must be evaluated before the risky expression to protect it.

quiz.prompt: Which operands are returned by these two Boolean expressions?
quiz.explanation: or returns its fallback when the first string is empty; and returns the falsey zero.

quiz.prompt: Which results distinguish a copied list value from the same object?
quiz.explanation: Each list expression creates a separate list, even though the contents compare equal.
quiz.code:
left = [1]
right = [1]
print(left == right, left is right)

quiz.prompt: Does the chain include its upper boundary of 100?
quiz.explanation: 100 is allowed by <=; 101 fails the upper comparison.

keyPoints.en: Comparison chains make range checks readable.
keyPoints.bn: চেইন তুলনা দিয়ে সীমার শর্ত সহজে পড়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: and and or evaluate only as far as needed.
keyPoints.bn: and আর or যতটুকু দরকার ততটুকুই যাচাই করে।

keyPoints.en: Equality compares values while identity compares objects.
keyPoints.bn: সমতা মান তুলনা করে, পরিচয় একই অবজেক্ট কি না দেখে।

keyPoints.en: Use is None when checking for a missing value.
keyPoints.bn: মান নেই কি না যাচাই করতে is None ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: String membership is case-sensitive substring searching.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্রিংয়ে সদস্যপদ যাচাইয়ের সময় অক্ষরের বড়-ছোট হাত আলাদা ধরা হয়।

examQuestions.question: Explain why a == b and a is b can disagree for two lists.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Two separate lists can contain equal values, so == returns True. They are still different objects, so is returns False. A second name assigned directly to one list shares its identity.

examQuestions.question: Explain short-circuit evaluation using a denominator check.
examQuestions.answerHtml: In denominator != 0 and numerator / denominator > 2, a zero denominator makes the left operand False. Python then skips the division. Reversing the order loses that protection.

examQuestions.question: Write an expression for a mark from 40 through 100, excluding invalid higher marks.
examQuestions.answerHtml: 40 <= mark <= 100 checks both inclusive boundaries. A mark of 101 is rejected even though it exceeds the pass threshold.
